P: $f(x)$ is continuous for all real values of $x$
Q: $f(x)$ is differentiable for all real values of $x$

questions.referenceAnswer: A group of order four either has an element of order four and is cyclic ($C_4$), or every nonidentity element has order two and it is $C_2\times C_2$. These two groups are Abelian and non-isomorphic, exhausting the possibilities.

questions.referenceAnswer: The iteration is Newton's method for $x^2-9/4=0$. Starting at 0.5 gives 2.5,1.7,1.5117647,... . For positive x the next value is at least 1.5 by AM-GM; above 1.5 it decreases and is bounded below. Its positive fixed point satisfies x/2=9/(8x), so x=1.5.

Consider a machine with a byte addressable main memory of $2^{16}$ bytes. Assume that a direct mapped data cache consisting of 32 lines of 64 bytes each is used in the system. A $50\times50$ two-dimensional array of bytes is stored in the main memory starting from memory location 1100 H. Assume that the data cache is initially empty. The complete array is accessed twice. Assume that the contents of the data cache do not change in between the two accesses.
How many data cache misses will occur in total?
questions.subject: 4. COA
questions.referenceAnswer: Assume the same sequential byte-address traversal on both complete passes, the intended array-access model. Address 0x1100 is line-aligned. The 2500-byte array occupies ceil(2500/64)=40 blocks. The first pass misses 40 times. In a 32-line direct cache its first eight blocks conflict with its last eight; the next pass misses on those first eight and last eight, totaling 40+16=56. The scan does not explicitly state traversal order, so C is retained as the sequential-pass reference and self-assessed.

Statement for Linked Answer Questions 84 and 85:
Suppose that a robot is placed on the Cartesian plane. At each step it is allowed to move either one unit up or one unit right, i.e., if it is at $(i,j)$ then it can move to either $(i+1,j)$ or $(i,j+1)$. How many distinct paths are there for the robot to reach the point $(10,10)$ starting from the initial position $(0,0)$?
questions.subject: 1. Discrete Maths
questions.referenceAnswer: Every path consists of 20 moves: ten right and ten up. Choose which ten of the 20 positions hold the right moves. The count is $\binom{20}{10}=184756$.

Statement for Linked Answer Questions 84 and 85:
Suppose that a robot is placed on the Cartesian plane. At each step it is allowed to move either one unit up or one unit right, i.e., if it is at $(i,j)$ then it can move to either $(i+1,j)$ or $(i,j+1)$. 
Suppose that the robot is not allowed to traverse the line segment from $(4,4)$ to $(5,4)$. With this constraint, how many distinct paths are there for the robot to reach $(10,10)$ starting from $(0,0)$?
questions.subject: 1. Discrete Maths
questions.referenceAnswer: Subtract paths using the forbidden directed edge. There are $\binom84=70$ prefixes to (4,4), one forbidden step, and $\binom{11}{5}=462$ suffixes from (5,4) to (10,10). Thus valid paths number $\binom{20}{10}-\binom84\binom{11}{5}=184756-32340=152416$.
